---
title: "Research"
subtitle: "Nanoscale devices and molecular transport"
---

My research focuses on fabricating and characterizing solid-state and hybrid nanopores, with particular attention to how pore geometry, material interfaces, and molecular structure influence ionic-current signals.

## Research projects

### DNA origami hybrid nanopores

DNA origami can be incorporated into a solid-state nanopore to modify its sensing environment. Our published work examined protein translocation measurements using this hybrid configuration. [Project details](projects/dna-origami.qmd).

### Multilayer heterostructure nanopores

Layered structures combining silicon nitride with two-dimensional materials provide a route to examine asymmetric molecular transport. [Project details](projects/heterostructures.qmd).

### α-Hemolysin hybrid nanopores

Ongoing research investigates biological pore integration with fabricated nanostructures. This work is at the research stage; unpublished results are not included here.

### Programmable nanopore fabrication

Automated electrical methods support controlled pore formation and experimental repeatability. [Project details](projects/instrumentation.qmd).

## Research methods

Solid-state nanopore fabrication, controlled dielectric breakdown, ionic-current acquisition, membrane heterostructures, experimental signal analysis, COMSOL modeling, and statistical learning.
